paper_title: VideoLLaMB Long-context Video Understanding with Recurrent Memory   Bridges
caption: GPU Memory Cost. We apply all the experiments on a single NVIDIA A800 GPU.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of frames and the GPU memory cost in gigabytes for several video generation models. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Frames,” displays a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1000, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 100, indicating frame increments. The y-axis, labeled “Memory (GB),” also employs a linear scale extending from approximately 150 to 400, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 50. The red line, represented by circular markers and a solid line style, shows a rapid decrease from a value of approximately 380 GB at 0 frames to approximately 230 GB at 400 frames. The dark orange line, indicated by square markers and a solid line style, increases from a value of approximately 75 GB at 0 frames to approximately 100 GB at 1000 frames. The teal line, visualized with circular markers and a solid line style, starts at approximately 65 GB at 0 frames and increases to approximately 95 GB at 1000 frames. The light blue line, depicted with circular markers and a solid line style, begins at approximately 40 GB at 0 frames and rises to approximately 80 GB at 1000 frames. Finally, the purple line, shown with circular markers and a solid line style, begins near 300 GB at 0 frames and decreases to approximately 350 GB at 400 frames.
